topic: Slicing and Polymorphism with Virtual Functions
explanation: When a derived class object is assigned to a base class object (or passed to a function expecting a base class), only the base class portion of the derived object is copied. This is called "slicing."  To avoid losing the derived class's specific data and behavior, we use polymorphism with virtual functions.  Polymorphism allows us to call the correct version of a function at runtime, even if the function is called through a base class pointer or reference. This is crucial for flexible and extensible object-oriented design.
keywords: Object slicing, Slicing C++, C++ slicing problem, Polymorphism virtual functions
